files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
### Added
- **A transaction can be split between several people at once.** The Share expense dialog only split with one contact at a time, either 50/50 or a typed amount, so a bill shared between three meant opening it once for each person and working out their share by hand, and reopening it on a split transaction only offered to add someone else. It now lists all of your contacts with a tick box each, plus a row for you, and splits **Equally**, **By percentage** or **By amount**, showing what each person owes as you go. You are in the split by default, and unticking your own row divides the whole amount between the others, for something you paid on their behalf. A penny that will not divide evenly stays with you. Reopening the dialog shows the splits already saved, which can be changed, added to, or removed by unticking everyone, and a split that has been settled is shown but locked, with what it covered left out of what there is to split. Suggested by @justinlimbo ([#391](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/391))
- **Project budgets.** A budget for a job that runs over months, such as a renovation, a wedding or a long trip, where a monthly budget that resets does not fit. A project covers a category and everything under it from a start date to an optional end date, with one total for the lot, and its subcategories can each be given an amount of their own, with what is left shown as unallocated. The new **Projects** page shows spent, remaining and how much of the time has gone for each project, and opens a breakdown per subcategory with a link to the transactions behind the figures. The spending is worked out the same way as on the Budget page, so refunds are taken off and split transactions count in the right subcategories. Creating a project can tick **Exclude from budgeting** on its category, so a big project bill does not show as over budget on the monthly Budget page. Projects can be shared with other Nextcloud users like savings goals, and anything the people you share the category with file under it counts towards the project. There is also a dashboard tile. Suggested by @justinlimbo ([#391](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/391))

- **A new category starts on a colour nothing else is using, and several categories can be recoloured at once.** Every new category opened on the same blue, so a budget of twenty meant choosing twenty colours by hand and checking each new one against the rest. New categories now take the next colour from a palette of 32 that none of your categories use yet, and once all 32 are in use the one used least often comes next. For categories that already exist there is a **Recolor** button beside **Delete Selected** on the Categories page: tick the ones to change, or use **Select All**, and each is given a different colour, avoiding the colours of the categories left unticked. Suggested by @fatino ([#392](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/392))

### Changed
- **Translations.** German and French have been updated from Weblate.

### Fixed
- **The red Delete Selected buttons can be read again.** Nextcloud paints a button marked as an error with dark red text on a red fill, so the label on **Delete Selected** in the accounts, transactions and categories lists was close to unreadable. Those three now use the app's own destructive red with white text, which also holds up on Nextcloud 30, where the error colour is a pale tint that white text disappears into
- **Deleting a contact removes what you split with them.** The confirmation said every shared expense with the contact would go, however only the contact itself was deleted. Its splits and settlements stayed behind, left out of every balance, and the transactions they belonged to kept a **Shared** badge that nothing could clear. Deleting a contact now removes its splits and settlements with it, and anything left behind by a contact deleted before this is cleared when you update ([#391](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/391))
- **Restoring a backup keeps each category's report and budget settings.** A backup saved **Exclude from reports**, **Exclude from budgeting** and envelope budgeting for every category, however restoring it never read them back, so every category came back counted in reports and budgets with envelope budgeting turned off. They now come back as they were exported, along with the month the envelope started from. A backup made before these settings existed restores as before ([#391](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/391))
- **Amber budget bars show their progress again.** A bar in the amber band showed empty: between 60% and 80% of a budget on the Budget page, and over 50% up to 80% on the dashboard's **Budget Progress** tile. A Nextcloud style for warnings outranked the amber fill and pushed it out of its bar. The fill now stays inside the bar ([#391](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/391))
- **Bills can be shared from the Sharing page again.** The **Configure** panel only listed your bills, recurring income and savings goals if you had opened those pages since loading the app, and a section with nothing to list is left out, so going straight to Sharing showed no Bills section at all and there was no way to share them. Recurring transfers were never listed either. The panel now loads all three itself, transfers included. It also leaves out accounts someone else has shared with you, which could not be shared on and made the whole Accounts section fail to save if one was ticked. Reported by @fatino ([#392](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/392))

### Security
- **A bill can only pay from, or into, an account you can post to.** Creating or editing a bill never checked the account it named, and a bill's payments are booked as that account's owner, so a bill could put payments into an account belonging to another user on the same Nextcloud, including one never shared with you or shared read-only. Bills now accept only your own accounts and ones shared with you at **Read & Write**, the same rule new transactions already follow. Editing a shared bill still leaves the account it already pays from as it is, even when that account was not shared with you
